title: Ephemeral Runlet Safety Hub: Secure, Simulated Runbooks-as-Tasks
creator: Ethan Park
description: We need a hardened runtime and UX component (the Ephemeral Runlet Safety Hub) that lets operators and support engineers execute small runbook fragments ("runlets") as guarded, ephemeral tasks. The hub should: 1) spawn short-lived sandboxed containers or isolated worker processes for each runlet execution; 2) enforce RBAC and KMS-backed secret access at the runlet boundary; 3) perform a policy lint and simulated dry-run before any stateful action; 4) capture structured provenance and telemetry for Console; and 5) provide automatic fallbacks to read-only simulation when safety checks fail. This ticket implements the core runtime and the API surface for creating, validating, and executing runlets, plus the instrumentation hooks required by Console rollouts and cost accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Can create and register a runlet manifest with typed inputs and a declared effect scope (read-only, safe-write, privileged).
Execution API launches an ephemeral worker container that runs with least privilege and times out after configured TTL (default 5m).
Policy linter rejects runlets that reference disallowed APIs or escalate privileges; rejected runs return a structured failure with remediation hints.
Dry-run mode runs the same code path but disallows external side effects; dry-run output matches real-run output format for diffing.
Secrets are fetched from customer KMS/HSM with per-runlet access tokens; no secret material is logged.
Console shows token-level telemetry: runlet latency, cost estimate, success rate, and provenance link to the exact runlet/version used.
Canary rollout to internal support team (50 users) with feature flag and auto-rollback on >3% error rate or SLO violation.
Security review completed and artifacts stored in the security vault.
plan: Design runlet manifest schema (typed inputs, declared effects, constraints) — owner: Product + Eng
Implement ephemeral worker pool with containerized sandboxes and TTL enforcement — owner: infra/runtime
Integrate RBAC/KMS checks at broker layer and implement short-lived access tokens — owner: security
Build policy linter + dry-run harness and attach to pre-exec hook — owner: runtime
Add structured provenance metadata emission to the telemetry pipeline and surface in Console — owner: observability
End-to-end QA: internal simulation, pentest quick pass, and load soak for high-concurrency runlets
Canary release to support, collect metrics, iterate on fail-mode UX and runbook authoring docs

telemetry_goals: Average runlet latency (p50/p95) under 400ms/1s in steady state
Dry-run to real-run divergence less than 1% for audited runlets
No plaintext secrets emitted in logs across all runs (0 incidents)
Canary error budget threshold: 3% errors over 1h window
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged internal deploy to staging; run synthetic workloads and pentest harness.
Phase 1: Canary to internal support (feature-flag: support-runlets=true) — 50 users for 72 hours.
Phase 2: Broader beta to all support orgs with a training doc and runlet author checklist.
Phase 3: GA behind org-level allowlist; integration with Dedicated and Private deployments scheduled after two successful cycles.
notes: Trade-off: container sandboxes cost more than process isolation but offer stronger syscall and network controls; chosen for initial MVP.
Decision: dry-run mirrors code path to maximize parity; we accept minor tokenization differences and mitigate via simulation tokens.
Follow-up: consider a cached-runlet binary format to reduce cold-starts if adoption exceeds 10k runs/day.
